statement: A mapping and gap list for an academic prototype. It makes no claim of compliance, conformity or certification with any framework named here, applies none of their audit rules, and is not legal advice.

coverage_meaning.evidenced: every cited control is implemented and its evidence passes today
coverage_meaning.partial: at least one cited control is implemented or partial, and something is missing
coverage_meaning.documented: no control cited, but a document records the intent (intent, not enforcement)
coverage_meaning.gap: applicable, and neither a working control nor a document exists, or only planned controls do
coverage_meaning.out_of_scope: not applicable to a software prototype with no operating organisation, staff or premises

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A (applicability mapping, Statement-of-Applicability style)

items.title: Policies for information security
items.note: The baseline and security architecture stand in for a policy set; nothing is management-approved.
items.accepted: A prototype has no management to approve a policy set.

items.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
items.note: Roles and action authority are finalised; every control has a named owner role.

items.title: Segregation of duties
items.note: Requester is never the approver; the executor and the verifier are independent identities.

items.title: Management responsibilities
items.note: The control concerns an operating organisation; this prototype has none.

items.title: Contact with authorities
items.note: The control concerns an operating organisation; this prototype has none.

items.title: Contact with special interest groups
items.note: The control concerns an operating organisation; this prototype has none.

items.title: Threat intelligence
items.note: The threat model is built from public framework knowledge; no threat-intelligence feed is consumed.
items.accepted: No feed is available to an academic prototype.

items.title: Information security in project management
items.note: Security work is registered tasks with acceptance and evidence; the phase 09 gate exists.

items.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
items.note: Data inventory (7 categories) and asset list in the threat model.

items.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
items.note: Roles bound what each identity may do; no acceptable-use policy for people exists.

items.title: Return of assets
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Classification of information
items.note: Privacy classification is a contract field on every observation; retention classes are enforced.

items.title: Labelling of information
items.note: Every event carries a truth label and a privacy classification, validated at ingestion.

items.title: Information transfer
items.note: Device mTLS, TLS to the database, code-plus-PKCE in the browser; Kafka, OPA and Keycloak links are still plain inside the platform network.

items.title: Access control
items.note: Default-deny endpoint authorization from one inventory; OPA as decision point.

items.title: Identity management
items.note: Keycloak for people, workload identity for services; the joiner-mover-leaver procedure is in `docs/security/ACCESS_REVIEW.md`.

items.title: Authentication information
items.note: Secrets generated at deployment, kept out of Git and rotated; the token never touches storage in the browser.

items.title: Access rights
items.note: Roles are provisioned from one place; a reviewable report of who holds what is generated.

items.title: Information security in supplier relationships
items.note: Dependencies and images pinned and signed; no supplier agreements exist for open-source components.
items.accepted: Open-source suppliers offer no agreements to negotiate.

items.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
items.note: No supplier agreements exist for the open-source components and free hosted services used.

items.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
items.note: Pinned locks, secret/dependency/image scanning in CI, SBOM, provenance and signing.

items.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
items.note: CI re-scans on every change; no periodic supplier review.

items.title: Information security for use of cloud services
items.note: GitHub Actions, Docker Hub and SonarQube Cloud are used with least-privilege tokens; no cloud-service risk assessment is recorded.

items.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
items.note: Platform incidents are correlated and recorded with an append-only history (P10.07); no human incident-response procedure is exercised.

items.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
items.note: Alerts (P10.04) become incidents with severity and an unverified hypothesis (P10.07).

items.title: Response to information security incidents
items.note: Bounded, policy-controlled remediation with escalation to a person (P10.08); no security-incident playbook beyond it.

items.title: Learning from information security incidents
items.note: Incident and remediation histories are kept append-only; no post-incident review process is run.
items.accepted: No operating history to learn from.

items.title: Collection of evidence
items.note: Tamper-evident hash-chained histories, redacted exports for the auditor role only.

items.title: Information security during disruption
items.note: Safe local behaviour on loss of central services; durable edge outbox; policy outage never approves.

items.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
items.note: A tested, encrypted backup and a real disaster restore exist (P11.05: RTO 203 s and RPO 2.3 s on a small data set); there is no scheduled or off-host backup; the edge buffers offline.

items.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
items.note: Requirements are identified as GDPR-oriented assumptions; no legal determination is made.
items.accepted: A legal question for qualified counsel, outside the prototype.

items.title: Intellectual property rights
items.note: Licences and attribution are reviewed in P13.05; only redistributable data is used.

items.title: Protection of records
items.note: Audit classes are never purged; retention per class is enforced.

items.title: Privacy and protection of PII
items.note: Minimisation at the edge, redaction, retention, role-limited evidence; DPIA-style review.

items.title: Independent review of information security
items.note: P09.10 and the runs on the target (P11.04, P09.09) are independent acceptance runs and phase 12 adds more; no external review exists.

items.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
items.note: CI gates and the verifiers check the platform's own rules; no external standard is applied.
items.accepted: No claim against any external standard is made or intended.

items.title: Documented operating procedures
items.note: Clean-start and resource instructions exist; operational runbooks are P13.04.

items.title: Screening
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Terms and conditions of employment
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Information security awareness, education and training
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Disciplinary process
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
items.note: The leaver and mover steps for operating roles are written (`ACCESS_REVIEW.md`); no employment exists to change.

items.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Remote working
items.note: A human-resources control; the prototype has no staff to screen, contract or discipline.

items.title: Information security event reporting
items.note: Platform events are alerted and correlated; no route exists for people to report events.

items.title: Physical security perimeters
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Physical entry
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Physical security monitoring
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Working in secure areas
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Clear desk and clear screen
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Equipment siting and protection
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Security of assets off-premises
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Storage media
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Supporting utilities
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Cabling security
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Equipment maintenance
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
items.note: A physical-premises control; the prototype runs on a development host and one lab host it does not own the premises of.

items.title: User endpoint devices
items.note: Operators use a browser; the console holds the token in memory only (CTL-43) but no endpoint is managed.

items.title: Privileged access rights
items.note: The only override (incident commander, SC-2) needs a justification and is audited; roles are reviewed.

items.title: Information access restriction
items.note: Default-deny per endpoint; the audit trail is readable by the auditor role only.

items.title: Access to source code
items.note: A private GitHub repository with least-privilege CI tokens.

items.title: Secure authentication
items.note: PKCE S256 only, strict token validation, lockout; MFA readiness is a Keycloak setting not enabled for the demo.

items.title: Capacity management
items.note: Resource budget, storage and retention alerts (P10.04); load, a measured ceiling and a 30-minute soak on the target (P11.06); no longer soak and no capacity plan.

items.title: Protection against malware
items.note: Image and dependency scanning, non-root read-only edge container; no endpoint anti-malware.
items.accepted: Container scanning is the relevant surface.

items.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
items.note: Trivy on the repository and images in CI, pinned dependencies, SBOM.

items.title: Configuration management
items.note: Pinned images and locks; configuration and migration drift alerts (P10.04).

items.title: Information deletion
items.note: Retention windows per class, aggregation before deletion.

items.title: Data masking
items.note: Recursive redaction in audit, logs and errors; privacy-zone suppression at the edge.

items.title: Data leakage prevention
items.note: Redaction and role-limited evidence; no network-level leakage prevention.
items.accepted: Out of scope for a single-host prototype.

items.title: Information backup
items.note: An encrypted, tested backup and a real restore exist (P11.05); a schedule, an off-host copy and custody of the key do not.

items.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
items.note: One node and one volume per store: nothing is redundant beyond the edge outbox, the broker's queue for the gateway and safe local behaviour; what happens in an outage of each component was measured (P11.05, P11.06).
items.accepted: Accepted for the laboratory: a single node is the scope of this project (docs/environment/RESOURCE_BUDGET.md); redundancy would be a different deployment.

items.title: Logging
items.note: Append-only audit and transition histories, redacted; time source partly consolidated.

items.title: Monitoring activities
items.note: 27 alert rules tested live, platform incident correlation, bounded remediation; model drift monitoring is not built.

items.title: Clock synchronization
items.note: The database clock stamps every audit row; the target host's time synchronization is neither configured by this deployment nor monitored.

items.title: Use of privileged utility programs
items.note: No privileged utilities are exposed by the platform; the host is a development machine.

items.title: Installation of software on operational systems
items.note: Only signed, provenance-attested artefacts are admitted by the release gate, and on the target the backend and frontend images that run are shown to be the signed ones (P11.03); the edge image is built on the host.

items.title: Networks security
items.note: Device mTLS with topic ACLs, TLS to the database, and default-deny network policy enforced on a real cluster with 19 positive and negative checks (P11.04); links between services inside the namespace are plain.

items.title: Security of network services
items.note: TLS on the broker and the database and rate limits at the API; the other service links are plain (CTL-11).

items.title: Segregation of networks
items.note: Trust zones TZ0-TZ8 are designed; on the cluster the NetworkPolicies were shown to isolate workloads, including a pod of another namespace from the database (P11.04).

items.title: Web filtering
items.note: No user web browsing is provided by the platform.

items.title: Use of cryptography
items.note: TLS 1.3 to the database, mTLS to devices, signed artefacts, rotated secrets; no key-management service.

items.title: Secure development life cycle
items.note: Registered tasks, tests, verifiers with evidence, CI gates.

items.title: Application security requirements
items.note: Closed schemas, validated inputs, headers, rate limits.

items.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
items.note: Default-deny, least privilege, fail closed, separation of demo control.

items.title: Secure coding
items.note: SonarQube Cloud, secret scanning and tests on every push.

items.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
items.note: Negative tests sit beside the positive ones in every verifier; the abuse-case acceptance run (P09.10) and the native checks on the target (P11.04) are done; CI has not yet run on a hosted runner.

items.title: Outsourced development
items.note: Development is not outsourced.

items.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
items.note: Scratch databases for verifiers; demo control cannot reach operations; no production exists.
items.accepted: A prototype has no production environment.

items.title: Change management
items.note: Every change goes through CI; model changes through verify-then-commit activation; no change board.

items.title: Test information
items.note: All test and training data is synthetic or open; no production personal data exists.

items.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
items.note: No independent audit testing is performed; verifiers run against scratch databases.

items.title: Organizational Context
items.note: Mission, safety boundary and stakeholder assumptions are documented.

items.title: Risk Management Strategy
items.note: Risk register with likelihood, impact, treatment, owner and residual risk computed from control state.

items.title: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
items.note: Roles and action authority; control owners.

items.title: Policy
items.note: Policy is code (OPA) for actions and endpoints; no management policy set.

items.title: Oversight
items.note: Auditor role with redacted evidence access.

items.title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
items.note: Locks, digests, scanning, SBOM, provenance, signing.

items.title: Asset Management
items.note: Data and asset inventories; device registry; SBOM.

items.title: Risk Assessment
items.note: 76 threats scored for likelihood, safety and security impact.

items.title: Improvement
items.note: Findings become registered tasks; residual risk recomputed on each control change.

items.title: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
items.note: OIDC/PKCE, default-deny endpoints, OPA, workload identity, access review procedure.

items.title: Awareness and Training
items.note: No staff to train; operator guidance is UX documentation.

items.title: Data Security
items.note: Transport protection, tamper-evident audit, redaction, retention, edge privacy.

items.title: Platform Security
items.note: Verified model activation, pinned and signed artefacts, hardened edge container; cluster hardening (admission, RBAC, no mounted tokens, network policy) was checked natively on the target (P11.04).

items.title: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
items.note: Safe degraded behaviour and edge buffering; outages of the gateway, Kafka, ingestion and PostgreSQL lost nothing under load and every component restart recovered (P11.05, P11.06); a tested backup exists but no schedule; single node.

items.title: Continuous Monitoring
items.note: Alert rules and probes tested live; runtime detection with Falco proven on the target cluster (P09.09); alerts are not routed to an operator.

items.title: Adverse Event Analysis
items.note: Alerts and detector anomalies are correlated into incidents with unverified hypotheses.

items.title: Incident Management
items.note: Incidents are opened, owned, escalated and resolved with a chained history.

items.title: Incident Analysis
items.note: Causal hypotheses are recorded and never asserted as fact; no forensic tooling.
items.accepted: Out of scope for a prototype.

items.title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
items.note: A breach procedure is written (P13.04) and its steps checked against real, independently-tested controls (Falco, audit export, secret rotation); the sequence as a whole and the notification channel are not live-drilled.

items.title: Incident Mitigation
items.note: Registered, bounded, verified remediation with escalation.

items.title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
items.note: Recovery is verified from alerts, not from the adapter; a database restore after the loss of its volume was rehearsed on the target (P11.05).

items.title: Incident Recovery Communication
items.note: No stakeholders to notify in a prototype.

frameworks.name: ETSI EN 303 645 (consumer IoT baseline, used as a device security profile)

items.title: No universal default passwords
items.note: Devices authenticate with per-device certificates, never a shared password.

items.title: Implement a means to manage reports of vulnerabilities
items.note: Findings become registered tasks; no public disclosure policy.

items.title: Keep software updated
items.note: Verify-then-commit model activation with rollback; signed artefacts; a rollout and a rollback of a bad image were tested on the target (P11.05); no over-the-air device update service.

items.title: Securely store sensitive security parameters
items.note: Secrets kept out of Git and rotated; no hardware secure element.

items.title: Communicate securely
items.note: Per-device mTLS with default-deny topic ACLs; TLS to the database.

items.title: Minimize exposed attack surfaces
items.note: Non-root, read-only, capability-dropped edge container; only the health port is exposed.

items.title: Ensure software integrity
items.note: Model hash verified at load; signed artefacts.

items.title: Ensure that personal data is secure
items.note: Privacy zones, ephemeral identities, k-anonymity floor, redaction.

items.title: Make systems resilient to outages
items.note: Durable ordered edge outbox, safe offline behaviour, verified remediation.

items.title: Examine system telemetry data
items.note: Bounded low-cardinality telemetry, alerts and a detector on it.

items.title: Make it easy for users to delete user data
items.note: Retention deletes by class; no data-subject deletion workflow is exercised.

items.title: Make installation and maintenance of devices easy
items.note: Documented clean start; no device provisioning UX.

items.title: Validate input data
items.note: Schema, identity and content validation at ingestion and API.

items.title: Identification and authentication control (IAC)
items.note: People through Keycloak, services by workload identity, devices by certificate.

items.title: Use control (UC)
items.note: Default-deny use control per endpoint and action class, four-eyes, single executor.

items.title: System integrity (SI)
items.note: Validated input, replay protection, model and artefact integrity.

items.title: Data confidentiality (DC)
items.note: Redaction and role-limited evidence; the broker and the database links are TLS, transport between the other platform services is plain.

items.title: Restricted data flow (RDF)
items.note: Zones and conduits are designed (TZ0-TZ8); enforcement in the cluster was tested natively (P11.04).

items.title: Timely response to events (TRE)
items.note: Audit trail, alerts, incident correlation, remediation within 30 s of an incident (measured in P10.09).

items.title: Resource availability (RA)
items.note: Degraded-mode behaviour and rate limits; load, outage and a 30-minute soak measured on one node (P11.06); no redundancy.

items.title: Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling
items.note: Threat model, trust zones and default-deny architecture.

items.title: Authentication
items.note: OIDC authorization code with PKCE, lockout, refresh rotation.

items.title: Session Management
items.note: Short-lived tokens held in memory; no cookie session.

items.title: Access Control
items.note: Default-deny per endpoint and per action, role-limited evidence.

items.title: Validation, Sanitization and Encoding
items.note: Closed request schemas, validated cursors and ranges, escaped search.

items.title: Stored Cryptography
items.note: Secrets rotation and signing; an encrypted backup (P11.05); no data-at-rest encryption of the database volume.

items.title: Error Handling and Logging
items.note: Redacted logs and error responses, append-only audit.

items.title: Data Protection
items.note: Redaction, retention, edge minimisation.

items.title: Communication
items.note: TLS to the database and device mTLS, proven on the target (P11.04); internal links partly plain.

items.title: Malicious Code
items.note: Scanning, SBOM and signing; no dedicated code-integrity review.

items.title: Business Logic
items.note: Four-eyes, execution-time policy, safety bounds, idempotency and replay protection.

items.title: Files and Resources
items.note: No file upload is offered; evidence exports are redacted.

items.title: API and Web Service
items.note: Versioned APIs, closed schemas, rate and size limits.

items.title: Configuration
items.note: Pinned images, security headers, strict CORS, configuration drift alerts.

items.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (2023)
items.note: Policy decides per route and role; evidence access is role-limited; agency scope on emergency records is P09.06's planned control.

items.title: Broken Authentication (2023)
items.note: Strict token validation; PKCE only.

items.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization (2023)
items.note: Closed response schemas and redaction.

items.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption (2023)
items.note: Rate limits, request-size limits.

items.title: Broken Function Level Authorization (2023)
items.note: Default-deny per endpoint; action class gates.

items.title: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows (2023)
items.note: Four-eyes, expiry, idempotency, audited override.

items.title: Server Side Request Forgery (2023)
items.note: The API makes no user-directed outbound requests.

items.title: Security Misconfiguration (2023)
items.note: Headers, CORS, pinned images, drift alerts.

items.title: Improper Inventory Management (2023)
items.note: One endpoint inventory drives authorization and the UI; unlisted routes are denied.

items.title: Unsafe Consumption of APIs (2023)
items.note: External integrations are simulated; inbound events are validated.

items.title: Culture, accountability and policy for AI risk
items.note: Human authority over consequential recommendations; named control owners.

items.title: Context, intended use and impact of each AI system
items.note: Model cards state purpose and limitations; data provenance and splits are recorded.

items.title: Testing and measurement of AI risk and trustworthiness
items.note: Baselines beside every model, held-out splits with a test ledger, wide intervals reported; drift and fairness monitoring are not built.

items.title: Prioritised treatment and response for AI risk
items.note: Staged activation with rollback; a model is served only if it beats the transparent baselines; drift response is planned.

items.title: Policies related to AI
items.note: AI and data controls are in the baseline; no management-approved AI policy.

items.title: Internal organization
items.note: Roles and authority are defined; no AI governance body.

items.title: Resources for AI systems
items.note: Data, compute and tooling resources are recorded in the resource budget and manifests.

items.title: Assessing impacts of AI systems
items.note: Safety, privacy and per-class performance are assessed; the fairness review is P12.04.

items.title: AI system life cycle
items.note: Reproducible training, model cards, verified activation and rollback.

items.title: Data for AI systems
items.note: Provenance, licences, split integrity, leakage checks, synthetic-versus-measured labelling.

items.title: Information for interested parties of AI systems
items.note: Model cards and acceptance targets state measured limits; user-facing disclosure is P13.03.

items.title: Use of AI systems
items.note: Recommendations need approval; remediation is bounded and verified.

items.title: Third-party and customer relationships
items.note: No third-party AI service or customer is involved.

frameworks.name: GDPR (reference points only; not legal advice)

items.title: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency
items.note: Lawful-purpose assumptions are written; no legal basis is determined.
items.accepted: A legal question for qualified counsel.

items.title: Purpose limitation
items.note: Each data category has a stated purpose checked against real fields.

items.title: Data minimisation
items.note: Aggregation and privacy zones at the edge; redaction downstream.

items.title: Storage limitation
items.note: Retention windows enforced per class.

items.title: Integrity and confidentiality
items.note: Transport protection, tamper-evident audit, redaction, role-limited evidence.

items.title: Data protection by design and by default
items.note: Privacy decisions are made at the edge and recorded in the inventory.

items.title: Records of processing activities
items.note: The data inventory records categories, purposes, access, retention and rights.

items.title: Security of processing
items.note: Technical measures as mapped above; a tested backup exists (P11.05) but no schedule.

items.title: Notification of a personal data breach
items.note: A breach procedure is written (P13.04), naming containment, scoping, exposure assessment and notification steps; the notification channel and timing commitment are not exercised, and no jurisdiction's legal deadline is claimed - a real deployment needs qualified counsel for that step.

items.title: Data protection impact assessment
items.note: A DPIA-style review of video, trajectory and location processing is written; no supervisory-authority consultation.

items.title: Data subject rights
items.note: A rights process is described per category; no workflow is exercised.
items.accepted: No data subjects exist in a synthetic prototype.
